source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.name: condition_omission

mx.teacher_note: The successive percentage rule also covers this: {'excluded_case': 'Single percentage change', 'reason': 'There is no successive-base decision.', so it is not an exception — on the item about Decide whether successive percentage changes must be.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: The answer is successive percentage because of the most obvious label, colour, size or printed number in the stem, without using 'Decide whether successive percentage changes must be applied one after' as the operative test.

mx.name: mechanism_conflation
mx.teacher_note: successive percentage is settled by running 'Decide when a percentage can be computed mentally by using benchmark': Benchmark percentages can be combined or scaled because percentages of the same value — on the item about Decide whether successive percentage changes must be.

intelligence.enrichment: Successive discounts, markups, increases, or decreases use the changed amount as the next base, so their effects are multiplied in order rather than simply added.
